findings.issue: The team cookie's format and parsing are implemented three times; the two inline client copies already diverge from the server's parseTeam (no lowercase/trim) and hardcode TEAM_SIZE/cookie name separately
findings.suggestion: Extract a client-safe src/lib/teamClient.ts (readTeam/writeTeam/TEAM_SIZE) and import it from both <script> blocks — Astro bundles TS imports in component scripts

findings.issue: Three near-identical hand-rolled fetch→DOMParser→replaceWith micro-routers, with inconsistent popstate handling (partial swap on home, location.reload() on the moves page)
findings.suggestion: Either adopt a single shared swap helper, or evaluate astro:transitions ClientRouter with fallback='none' (the no-transitions spec constraint can be met with transition:none)

findings.issue: Non-OK upstream responses throw and no page catches them, so any API hiccup surfaces as an unhandled 500
findings.suggestion: Catch at the page boundary (or in api()) and render a small error state/500 page

findings.issue: Cache Map is unbounded and SWR refresh failures are silently swallowed while resetting the freshness timestamp (stale served, retry only after 60s)
findings.suggestion: Add an entry cap or LRU eviction, and log (or propagate) refresh failures instead of silently resetting hit.at

findings.location: app/src/components/MovesSection.astro:10 (pattern repeats in app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:48,60 and app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:27)
findings.issue: API payloads typed as any throughout, undermining astro/tsconfigs/strict
findings.suggestion: Add a small src/lib/types.ts for the PokeAPI shapes actually consumed (Named, Localized, Species, Pokemon, Move, Type)

findings.issue: noscript form action="#moves" drops the fragment on a GET submit, so the no-JS fallback lands at the page top
findings.suggestion: Point the action at the current pathname and rely on the fragment, or accept the minor noscript-only deviation

findings.issue: getSpeciesById and getHomeEntries rebuild 1k+-entry Maps/arrays on every request from cached lists
findings.suggestion: Cache the derived structures alongside the raw lists (data changes arrive via the SWR refresh anyway, so recompute when the list entry refreshes)

summary: A well-structured Astro 7 SSR app: canonical routing, config, cookies and response APIs, a genuinely good SWR data layer, and unusually careful client interaction code. The notable cross-file problems are the triplicated team-cookie logic (with drift between the copies), three hand-rolled partial-navigation scripts where the framework offers ClientRouter, unhandled upstream API errors, and pervasive any-typing. I'd merge after one round of small, mostly mechanical changes.
